source_text:
Ὡς οὐκ ἔστιν ἴσος ὁ ζυγὸς, βαροῦντος
τοῦ ἑνὸς μέρους, οὕτως οὐκ ἔστι κατορθῶσαι ἐντολὴν Θεοῦ, κατακρατοῦντος τοῦ
σαρκικοῦ φρονήματος Ὥσπερ οὐκ ἔστι μαθεῖν τέχνην, μὴ σχολάσαντα ἐπιμελῶς,
οὕτως οὐκ ἔστι κτήσασθαι προσευχὴν μὴ προσκαρτερήσαντα τῷ Θεῷ ἐν εὐθείᾳ
καρδίᾳ. Ὁ μὴ κεκτημένος προσευχὴν καθαρὰν, οὐκ ἔχει ὅπλον εἰς πόλεμον.
Ὁ κεκοσμημένος, καὶ σεσαρωμένος ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ, κατοικητήριον ἔσται
δαιμόνων. 79.1237 Ὡς οὐκ ἔστι κατοικῆσαι βασιλέα ἐν οἴκῳ πένητος, οὕτως οὐ
κατοικήσει Χριστὸς ἐν ψυχῇ ῥερυπωμένῃ ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας. Ὥσπερ ἀνήμερος τόπος
ἡμεροῦται δι' ἐπιμελοῦς φιλεργίας, οὕτως ψυχὴ ἀγριωθεῖσα ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις
ἠμεροῦται, εἰ νόμῳ Θεοῦ πολιτεύσεται. Ὥσπερ πέτρα οὖσα ἐν θαλάσσῃ ἑδραία μένει,
καὶ ἀσάλευτος κατακρουομένη ὑπὸ κυμάτων, οὕτω καὶ ὁ τὰς ἀρετὰς κατορθώσας,
καὶ ταύταις ὅλως ἀνακραθεὶς, οὐ μὴ σαλευθῇ ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου. Ὥσπερ ἰατρὸς πρὸς
τὴν τοῦ πάθους θεραπείαν ἐπινοεῖ τὸ φάρμακον, οὕτως καὶ ἡ γνῶσις τοῦ Θεοῦ
συντηρουμένη διδάσκει τὸν μετέχοντα αὐτῆς, ὅπως ἂν διαφυλαχθῇ, καὶ ἐπὶ μείζονα
προέλθοι. Ὥσπερ χαράδρα ἑαυτῆς ἐμποιεῖται τὴν διόδον οὕτω καὶ ἁμαρτία
παραδεχθεῖσα κατεργάζεται τοῦ κεκτημένου αὐτῆς τὴν ἀπώλειαν. Ὡς οὐκ ἔστιν εἰς
λίνα ἐμπεσόντα ἔλαφον εὐχερῶς ἐκφυγεῖν, οὕτως οὐ μὴ φύγῃ ἁμαρτίαν ὁ τὰς
ἐπιθυμίας ἐκτελῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ ἀναστρεφόμενος· ἐπιθυμίαι γὰρ
πονηραὶ, καὶ ἡδοναὶ, σειραὶ δύσλυτοι.
thought_title: No commandment, prayer, or virtue without effort; sin and desire ensnare
orientation: Evagrius continues his chain of comparisons, now showing that keeping God's commandment, acquiring prayer, and standing firm in virtue all require effort, while sin and desire trap the one who accepts them.
pass_a_gloss: As the yoke is not equal, when one side weighs down, so it is not possible to set right a commandment of God, when the fleshly mind prevails. Just as it is not possible to learn a craft, without having devoted oneself carefully, so it is not possible to acquire prayer without having persevered with God in uprightness of heart. The one who has not acquired pure prayer does not have a weapon for war. The one adorned and swept clean from the virtues of God will be a dwelling place of demons. 79.1237 As it is not possible for a king to dwell in a poor man's house, so Christ will not dwell in a soul defiled from sin. Just as a wild place is tamed through careful love of labor, so a soul made wild by sins is tamed, if it will conduct itself by the law of God. Just as a rock being in the sea remains firm and unshaken, being struck by waves, so also the one who has set right the virtues, and has been wholly mixed with them, will never be shaken by the devil. Just as a physician for the healing of the suffering devises the remedy, so also the knowledge of God, being preserved, teaches the one who partakes of it, how he might be kept safe, and might advance to greater things. Just as a ravine makes for itself the passage, so also sin, when admitted, works out the destruction of the one who possesses it. As it is not possible for a deer that has fallen into nets to escape easily, so the one who carries out the desires, and conducts himself in this world, will never escape sin; for evil desires and pleasures are bonds hard to loosen.

choices.why: φρόνημα is the mind-set or way of thinking; 'fleshly mind' keeps the noun force and the Pauline sense of a mindset opposed to God.
εὐθεῖα means straight or upright; the phrase echoes Psalm language about a right heart before God.

choices.term: κεκοσμημένος, καὶ σεσαρωμένος ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ
choices.english: adorned and swept clean from the virtues of God
choices.why: ἀπό with the passive participle indicates the source or agent of the sweeping; the person is swept clean by God's virtues, not emptied of them.
rejected: adorned and swept clean of God's virtues
adorned and swept clean by God's virtues

choices.why: ἀπό marks the source of the defilement; the soul is defiled as a result of sin, keeping the literal preposition.
δύσλυτος means hard to untie or dissolve; 'bonds hard to loosen' preserves the literal difficulty of release.

pass_b_english: Just as a scale cannot balance when one side is weighed down, so no one can accomplish God's commandment while the fleshly mind prevails over him. Just as no one can learn a craft without devoting himself to it diligently, so no one can acquire prayer without persevering before God in uprightness of heart. The one who has not acquired pure prayer has no weapon for battle. The one adorned and swept clean, yet devoid of God's virtues, will be a dwelling for demons. Just as a king cannot dwell in a poor man's house, so Christ will not dwell in a soul defiled from sin. Just as wild land is tamed through diligent cultivation, so a soul made wild by sins is tamed if it will conduct itself by God's law. Just as a rock in the sea remains firm and unshaken when battered by waves, so the one who has accomplished the virtues and been wholly mixed with them will never be shaken by the devil. Just as a physician devises a remedy for the healing of a disease, so the knowledge of God, when preserved, teaches the one who partakes of it how to be kept safe and advance to greater things. Just as a ravine makes its own passage, so sin, once admitted, brings about the destruction of the one who possesses it. Just as a deer that has fallen into nets cannot easily escape, so the one who carries out his desires and lives in this world will not escape sin; for evil desires and pleasures are bonds hard to loosen.

problems.quote: swept clean from the virtues of God
problems.source_quote: κεκοσμημένος, καὶ σεσαρωμένος ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ
problems.why: ἀπό with genitive means 'by' or 'with' virtues, not 'from' virtues; sense is adorned and swept clean BY God's virtues.
problems.fix: adorned and swept clean by the virtues of God

edits.old: adorned and swept clean from the virtues of God
edits.new: adorned and swept clean by the virtues of God

fixed: Changed 'from' to 'by' in 'adorned and swept clean from the virtues of God' because ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ means 'by the virtues of God' (instrumental/causal), not 'from the virtues'.

problems.quote: The one who has been adorned and swept clean by the virtues of God will become a dwelling place of demons.
problems.source_quote: Ὁ κεκοσμημένος, καὶ σεσαρωμένος ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ, κατοικητήριον ἔσται δαιμόνων.
problems.why: ἀπό with genitive means 'away from,' not 'by'—the Greek says swept clean *from* (i.e., of) virtues, not *by* virtues. The sense is ironic: one merely adorned/emptied of virtues becomes demonic dwelling.
problems.fix: The one adorned and swept clean of God's virtues will become a dwelling place of demons.

edits.old: adorned and swept clean by the virtues of God
edits.new: adorned and swept clean of the virtues of God

fixed: Changed 'by the virtues of God' to 'of the virtues of God' because ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ means 'away from the virtues of God,' i.e., swept clean of them, not by them.

problems.quote: swept clean of the virtues of God
problems.source_quote: κεκοσμημένος, καὶ σεσαρωμένος ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ
problems.why: ἀπό + genitive means 'from' not 'of'; the Greek says swept clean *from* (i.e., free from) God's virtues, meaning devoid of them, not cleaned of them.
problems.fix: adorned and swept clean of God's virtues (i.e., devoid of them)

problems.quote: The one who has been adorned and swept clean of the virtues of God will become a dwelling place of demons
problems.source_quote: Ὁ κεκοσμημένος, καὶ σεσαρωμένος ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ, κατοικητήριον ἔσται δαιμόνων
problems.why: The Greek is sarcastic/ironic: 'adorned and swept clean' (like a decorated empty house) *from* (without) virtues becomes a demon's dwelling. English 'of' misreads ἀπό and loses the irony.
problems.fix: The one adorned and swept clean, yet devoid of God's virtues, will be a dwelling for demons
problems.ruling: ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ means 'deprived of God's virtues'; 'of' misreads ἀπό, reversing meaning: virtueless soul becomes demon's dwelling

edits.old: The one who has been adorned and swept clean of the virtues of God will become a dwelling place of demons.
edits.new: The one adorned and swept clean, yet devoid of God's virtues, will be a dwelling for demons.

fixed: Changed 'adorned and swept clean of the virtues of God' to 'adorned and swept clean, yet devoid of God's virtues' to render ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν Θεοῦ as 'from/without God's virtues' and preserve the ironic sense of the Greek.

dismissed.why: Source says adorned/swept clean FROM virtues; English flips to 'devoid of' virtues.
dismissed.note: Σεσαρωμένος ἀπὸ ἀρετῶν means 'swept clean of the virtues' (compare Matthew 12:44), so 'devoid of God's virtues' is right; the suggested fix gets the meaning backwards.
